model_annotation: This horizontal stacked bar chart illustrates government expenditure as a percentage of GDP (labeled "% des BIP") for 22 European countries, showing both the baseline spending level in 2021 and the increase between 2021 and 2024. The vertical axis lists countries from top to bottom, and the horizontal axis displays values on a linear scale ranging from 0 to approximately 4.0, with major tick marks at 0, 1, 2, 3, and 4. Each bar is composed of two stacked segments: a light green segment representing "Ausgaben 2021" (expenditure in 2021) and a blue segment representing "Anstieg zwischen 2021 und 2024" (increase between 2021 and 2024), with the blue portion appearing on the left side of each bar and the green portion extending to the right. Additionally, a black marker (short vertical line) for each country indicates "1,5 % über dem Referenzwert von 2021" (1.5% above the reference value of 2021). The countries are sorted in descending order by total bar length, with Polen at the top showing the longest combined bar at approximately 4.0% of GDP (with roughly 2.3% in blue increase and 1.7% in green baseline), followed by Estland at approximately 3.5%, Lettland at approximately 3.2%, and Litauen at approximately 3.1%. At the bottom of the chart, Spanien has the shortest total bar at approximately 1.1%, preceded by Luxemburg at approximately 1.2%, Slowenien at approximately 1.2%, and Belgien at approximately 1.2%. Countries in the middle range include Finnland at approximately 2.7%, Dänemark at approximately 2.5%, Rumänien at approximately 2.4%, Bulgarien at approximately 2.2%, Schweden at approximately 2.1%, Deutschland at approximately 2.0%, Ungarn at approximately 1.9%, Tschechien at approximately 1.9%, Frankreich at approximately 2.0%, Niederlande at approximately 1.9%, Slowakei at approximately 1.9%, Portugal at approximately 1.6%, and Italien at approximately 1.6%. The black reference markers vary in position across countries, appearing at approximately 3.9% for Polen, 3.5% for Estland, and progressively lower values for countries further down the list, with Luxemburg's marker at approximately 2.3% and Spanien's at approximately 2.2%. No bars appear to be individually emphasized through bolding or outlining beyond the consistent color-coding scheme applied throughout.
